{"id": "fdbeebaa-577f-4046-ae75-0b05373c183a", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_VDzu5gk9sXzIwPLQ29JFdN", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: storage-ebs-expertise\\\\ndescription: >\\\\n  Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an\\\\n  EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only\\\\n  say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS. Use it for\\\\n  alarms on AWS/EBS metrics (VolumeReadOps, VolumeWriteOps, VolumeReadBytes,\\\\n  VolumeWriteBytes, VolumeQueueLength, VolumeTotalReadTime/WriteTime,\\\\n  VolumeAvgReadLatency, BurstBalance) or EBSIOBalance%/EBSByteBalance%; for sizing\\\\n  IOPS or throughput changes; for a volume modification that looks stuck or failed;\\\\n  for deciding which snapshots or AMIs are safe to delete or how to recover them;\\\\n  for KMS errors on encrypted volumes; for EBS quota or limit errors; for a jump in\\\\n  the EBS bill; and for a pre-launch EBS review. Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx,\\\\n  instance store, or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS KMS, AWS CloudTrail, Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes. Troubleshoot mode answers \\\\\"something is wrong, why?\\\\\" through one of five paths and returns a fixed verdict. Review mode answers \\\\\"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\\\\\" and returns a rated report. Both modes are read-only and share the same volume-type rules, instance limits and service rules. Load only the reference files the request needs.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\n\\\\n- Storage-related slowness, timeouts or high I/O latency on an Amazon EC2 instance.\\\\n- An alarm on AWS/EBS metrics or on instance `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%`.\\\\n- A volume modification that looks stuck, failed, or did not improve performance.\\\\n- Snapshot, AMI, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Backup or Recycle Bin questions, including which snapshots are safe to delete.\\\\n- Encrypted-volume access errors and AWS KMS questions for Amazon EBS.\\\\n- Amazon EBS cost increases, idle or over-provisioned volumes.\\\\n- An operation that failed on an Amazon EBS quota, or \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\"\\\\n- A request to review Amazon EBS posture before a launch, migration or peak event.\\\\n\\\\nDo not use this skill for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, instance store, or Amazon EC2 issues unrelated to Amazon EBS.\\\\n\\\\n## Prerequisites\\\\n\\\\n- Read-only permissions for the APIs listed in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md).\\\\n- AWS CloudTrail access is optional. The skill works without it.\\\\n- Mutating changes run only through directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App), which need their own role and operator approval on the approval card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Run the path and draft the report\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Check the draft, fix it, then present it\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Classify the Request\\\\n\\\\n| The user says or the alarm shows | Mode and path | Load |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| \\\\\"My app is slow\\\\\", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics, `EBSIOBalance%` or `EBSByteBalance%`, \\\\\"is it storage?\\\\\", \\\\\"how much IOPS do I need?\\\\\" | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"My modification is stuck\\\\\", \\\\\"the new IOPS has not taken effect\\\\\", a `ModifyVolume` error, resize, gp2 to gp3, extend the file system, shrink or cancel | Troubleshoot: volume modification | [references/troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](references/troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Which snapshots can I delete?\\\\\", snapshot copy did not arrive, AMI creation stuck, recover a deleted snapshot or volume, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, Recycle Bin | Troubleshoot: snapshots | [references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md](references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"I can\\'t attach my KMS-encrypted volume\\\\\", share an encrypted snapshot or AMI, encryption by default, re-encrypt a volume | Troubleshoot: encryption | [references/troubleshoot-encryption.md](references/troubleshoot-encryption.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Why did my EBS bill go up?\\\\\", unexplained charges, idle or unattached volumes, pricing model | Troubleshoot: billing | [references/troubleshoot-billing.md](references/troubleshoot-billing.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Limit exceeded\\\\\", a quota error, \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\" | Shared capability: quota headroom | [Capacity and quota headroom](references/review-operational.md#capacity-and-quota-headroom) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Are my volumes backed up?\\\\\" | Review: resilience area | [Resilience](references/review-operational.md#resilience) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Review my EBS setup\\\\\", \\\\\"is my storage production-ready?\\\\\" | Review | [references/review-operational.md](references/review-operational.md) and [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md) |\\\\n\\\\nIf a request fits more than one row, answer the question the user asked first and treat the rest as Separate findings.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Load the Shared References\\\\n\\\\n- Always load [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md) (read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks).\\\\n- Load [references/metrics-thresholds.md](references/metrics-thresholds.md) for any metric judgement.\\\\n- Load [references/finding-logic.md](references/finding-logic.md) for the verdict, the binding layer, escalation and review ratings.\\\\n- Load [references/ebs-best-practices.md](references/ebs-best-practices.md) for service rules (Elastic Volumes, instance limits, quotas, snapshots, quirks).\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Run the Path and Draft the Report\\\\n\\\\nFollow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs. Then draft the report in the format below.\\\\n\\\\n### Troubleshoot verdict format\\\\n\\\\n1. **Answer:** the asked question, answered first.\\\\n2. **Evidence:** values with units and time window.\\\\n3. **Binding layer:** Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment, or Not applicable.\\\\n4. **Recommendation:** exact parameters, or \\\\\"No change\\\\\".\\\\n5. **Separate findings:** other true facts that do not change the Answer.\\\\n6. **Gaps:** what could not be checked and why.\\\\n\\\\nReview mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md). Every review answer starts with its Summary table, which rates all six areas (capacity and quota headroom, observability, cost hygiene, resilience, encryption posture, deletion protection), even when an area has no findings or is `Indeterminate`.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It\\\\n\\\\nReview the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every \\\\\"safe to delete\\\\\" verdict is backed by the checks its tier requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not safe to delete.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, DeleteSnapshot, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed \\\\\"approve\\\\\" in chat is not approval.\\\\n- **Discover, don\\'t assume:** read every configuration value from the APIs.\\\\n- **Rule EBS in or out before tuning it.**\\\\n- **Answer the asked question first;** other findings go under \\\\\"Separate findings\\\\\".\\\\n- **Always check the instance layer** and size changes within the instance\\'s EBS **baseline**.\\\\n- **Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.**\\\\n- **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. AWS CloudTrail is optional; `DescribeVolumesModifications` is the change record.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). Name every failed API under Gaps and continue with the rest.\\\\n\\\\n## References\\\\n\\\\n- [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md): performance attribution, the live-tested procedure\\\\n- [references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md](references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md): safe-to-delete tiers, copy, AMI, lifecycle and recovery\\\\n- {"id": "3ca30d1b-20cb-42b6-a606-8bab01ac9b0a", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_4PvAnNYmfcchNnxBa3Ltfn", "content": "[{'text': '# Review mode: Amazon EBS operational review\\n\\nReview mode answers \"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\". It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification).\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Do not infer criticality from tag values by yourself.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical volume with no Amazon EBS alarm is `Medium`. `High` if the operator says the volume backs a production database or service. An alarm in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for a long time is `Low` (it may be on a deleted volume).\\n\\n**Fix**: propose alarms with metric, dimensions (`VolumeAvg*` need `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`) and the threshold the operator chooses.\\n\\n## Cost hygiene\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. gp2 volumes: gp3 candidates. gp3 has 20% lower price per GiB than gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.\\n2. Unattached volumes: `DescribeVolumes` with `status=available`.\\n3. Over-provisioned IOPS or throughput: measured vs provisioned, and provisioned above the instance EBS baseline (see [troubleshoot-billing.md](troubleshoot-billing.md) step 6).\\n4. AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n\\n**Rating rule**: `Low` by default. `Medium` when the operator names cost as a goal or the resource is large relative to the account\\'s Amazon EBS spend as shown in Cost Explorer.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyVolume` to gp3 with IOPS and throughput sized as in [troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) step 6; snapshot then delete for unattached volumes. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Resilience\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. Inventory volumes (`DescribeVolumes`), including root volumes.\\n2. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: `GetLifecyclePolicies` (state `ENABLED`) and `GetLifecyclePolicy` for target tags and resource type. Target tags are case sensitive. Note default policies, which target the Region\\'s volumes or instances without recent backups.\\n3. AWS Backup: `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection` (selection by resource ARN, by tag condition, or all resources of a type), and `ListProtectedResources`.\\n4. Match each volume to a policy or a selection. A volume that matches none is unprotected.\\n5. For protected volumes, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true for the latest recovery point, and the latest `aws:dlm:*` tagged snapshot of the volume. Compare its age with the policy schedule. Without that parameter, the call also returns manual snapshots, which are not backups from the plan.\\n6. Cross-Region copy for disaster recovery: copy actions in DLM policies or AWS Backup copy rules.\\n7. Ask the operator for their recovery point objective. Do not assume one.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: an unprotected volume the operator calls critical is `High`. A protected volume whose latest recovery point is older than its own schedule is `High` (the backup may be failing). No cross-Region copy where the operator needs Regional disaster recovery is `Medium`. Unprotected non-critical volumes are `Low`.\\n\\n**Fix**: tag the volume to match an existing policy, add it to a backup selection, or create a policy. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Encryption posture\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region.\\n2. Unencrypted volumes and snapshots (`Encrypted` is false).\\n3. For keys in use, AWS KMS `DescribeKey` state. A disabled or pending-deletion key in use is a risk.\\n4. Snapshot exposure: `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState` per Region, and `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all` for snapshots that are public now.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a key in use that is disabled or pending deletion is `High`. A public snapshot is `High`. Encryption by default off is `Medium`. Unencrypted volumes are `Medium`, or `High` if the operator says the data is regulated. Snapshot block public access in the `unblocked` state is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: turn on encryption by default; re-encrypt with the steps in [troubleshoot-encryption.md](troubleshoot-encryption.md); turn on snapshot block public access (`block-all-sharing`, or `block-new-sharing` while existing public shares are reviewed). All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Deletion protection\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeInstanceAttribute --attribute blockDeviceMapping` for `DeleteOnTermination` on each attached volume. A data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is deleted when the instance terminates.\\n2. Recycle Bin `ListRules` for `EBS_SNAPSHOT` (and for AMIs if the account uses them).\\n3. Snapshot lock: `DescribeLockedSnapshots` for snapshots the operator must keep.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is `High`. No Recycle Bin rule for snapshots is `Medium`. No lock on snapshots the operator says are compliance records is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyInstanceAttribute` to set `DeleteOnTermination` false on the data volume, a Recycle Bin retention rule, or a snapshot lock. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- Review mode is entirely read-only. It never runs a mutating call.\\n- Every fix is listed under \"Proposed actions\" in the report with exact parameters, expected effect, cost direction and rollback. 3. Put the critical volumes under AWS Backup or DLM, with a schedule based on your RPO.

A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. All 9 non-root attached volumes (and the other 9 roots) have the values shown above. All non-root attached volumes have `DeleteOnTermination=false`, so no data volume is deleted on termination. That makes no High finding here.

## Not checked
- **Resilience:** DLM, AWS Backup and Recycle Bin were not queried. Another agent covers them.
- **Compute Optimizer** (`GetEBSVolumeRecommendations`) and **Cost Explorer**: not called, so there are no spend figures or right-sizing recommendations.
- **Per-volume metrics:** `VolumeQueueLength`, latency and `BurstBalance` were not queried. I used instance-level EBS metrics only.
- **Stopped instances:** the measured peaks come from the periods when they ran. Their volume metrics reflect eval workloads, not production.
- **Other checks not run:** composite alarms, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, instance termination protection, and other Regions.
- **Gated or failed APIs:** none.
- **Not verified:** `DescribeInstances` shows `EbsOptimized=false` for the c6i.xlarge and the t3.micro i-0123456789abcdef0_4, although `DescribeInstanceTypes` lists EBS optimization as `default` for both types. I did not look into it.

## Proposed actions
None were executed. Each would need a directed action approved on the approval card.
1. Enable `EnableEbsEncryptionByDefault` in us-east-1. Cost impact: none, since the AWS-managed key is free.
2. `EnableSnapshotBlockPublicAccess` with `block-all-sharing`. Rollback is `DisableSnapshotBlockPublicAccess`.
3. Add EBS alarms, as in Observability, for the volumes the operator names as critical.
4. Right-size IOPS and throughput on vol-0123456789abcdef0_5 and vol-0123456789abcdef0_24, or resize the instances.
5. Convert gp2 volumes to gp3 with `ModifyVolume`. Rollback is another `ModifyVolume`, limited to 4 modifications per volume per 24 hours.
6. Snapshot and delete the unattached volumes once the operator confirms they are not needed.

## Questions for the operator
- Which volumes are critical, or which tags identify them?
- Is any data regulated?
- Do you need snapshot retention locks?
- Do the `ebs-eval-*` and `ebs-workshop-*` resources go away before launch?

{"id": "18f077c3-9a68-4262-b9c0-6be12fc61786", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_yIz5Ko0WJ2rrGIjfyV7jrL", "content": "[{'text': '# Review mode: Amazon EBS operational review\\n\\nReview mode answers \"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\". It is entirely read-only. Run each area per Region, rate each finding with the scale in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md), and write the report with [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\nThe Capacity and quota headroom section is also a shared capability. Troubleshoot paths use it when an operation failed on a limit.\\n\\n## Capacity and quota headroom\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\nRun every check below even when the error looks simple. A user who reports a quota error has already failed to fix it alone, so give documented findings in the verdict format, not a short chat reply. Whether the run is a chat or a formal investigation is decided by how the user starts it, not by this skill.\\n\\n1. If an operation failed, quote the error and name the quota it refers to. For example \"You have exceeded your maximum io2 IOPS limit of 100000 IOPS in this region\" refers to the regional io2 IOPS quota, which is separate from the per-volume maximum.\\n2. `ListServiceQuotas --service-code ebs`: quota name, code, applied `Value`, `Adjustable`. Find quotas by name; never hardcode codes. `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota` shows the default.\\n3. Compute usage from the inventory:\\n   - Provisioned IOPS: sum of `Iops` for io1 volumes and for io2 volumes, separately.\\n   - Storage per type: sum of `Size` per volume type, converted from GiB to TiB.\\n   - Snapshots per Region: count of `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self`.\\n   - Fast snapshot restore: `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores` count of enabled entries.\\n4. `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` for pending requests. Never propose a duplicate.\\n\\n**Rating rule**\\n\\n- Usage at or above 80% of the applied quota is flagged. The 80% value is configurable; ask the operator if they use a different one.\\n- A quota that blocked an operation is `High`.\\n- A quota flagged at or above the threshold is `Medium`, or `High` if the user states a planned increase that would exceed it.\\n- Unreadable quota or usage is `Indeterminate`.\\n\\n**Fix**\\n\\n- Adjustable: a pre-filled Service Quotas request (service code `ebs`, quota code as read, desired value) proposed as a directed action. The desired value is the user\\'s stated need, or current usage plus the request that failed. No fixed multipliers.\\n- Not adjustable: draft the AWS Support case text (service, quota name, Region, desired value, business justification).\\n- Name the quotas that commonly cause problems: per-Region IOPS for io1 and io2, per-Region storage per volume type, snapshots per Region, and fast snapshot restore.\\n\\n## Observability\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EBS namespace: alarms on `VolumeQueueLength`, latency (`VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency`, or `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeTotalWriteTime` math), throughput, and `BurstBalance` for gp2, st1 and sc1.\\n2. `DescribeAlarms` for the AWS/EC2 namespace: `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` on instances that publish them.\\n3. Which volumes are critical: ask the operator, or use tags they name. Do not infer criticality from tag values by yourself.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical volume with no Amazon EBS alarm is `Medium`. `High` if the operator says the volume backs a production database or service. An alarm in `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` for a long time is `Low` (it may be on a deleted volume).\\n\\n**Fix**: propose alarms with metric, dimensions (`VolumeAvg*` need `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`) and the threshold the operator chooses.\\n\\n## Cost hygiene\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. gp2 volumes: gp3 candidates. gp3 has 20% lower price per GiB than gp2 and includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s.\\n2. Unattached volumes: `DescribeVolumes` with `status=available`.\\n3. Over-provisioned IOPS or throughput: measured vs provisioned, and provisioned above the instance EBS baseline (see [troubleshoot-billing.md](troubleshoot-billing.md) step 6).\\n4. AWS Compute Optimizer `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` if enabled (optional).\\n\\n**Rating rule**: `Low` by default. `Medium` when the operator names cost as a goal or the resource is large relative to the account\\'s Amazon EBS spend as shown in Cost Explorer.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyVolume` to gp3 with IOPS and throughput sized as in [troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) step 6; snapshot then delete for unattached volumes. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Resilience\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. Inventory volumes (`DescribeVolumes`), including root volumes.\\n2. Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: `GetLifecyclePolicies` (state `ENABLED`) and `GetLifecyclePolicy` for target tags and resource type. Target tags are case sensitive. Note default policies, which target the Region\\'s volumes or instances without recent backups.\\n3. AWS Backup: `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection` (selection by resource ARN, by tag condition, or all resources of a type), and `ListProtectedResources`.\\n4. Match each volume to a policy or a selection. A volume that matches none is unprotected.\\n5. For protected volumes, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true for the latest recovery point, and the latest `aws:dlm:*` tagged snapshot of the volume. Compare its age with the policy schedule. Without that parameter, the call also returns manual snapshots, which are not backups from the plan.\\n6. Cross-Region copy for disaster recovery: copy actions in DLM policies or AWS Backup copy rules.\\n7. Ask the operator for their recovery point objective. Do not assume one.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: an unprotected volume the operator calls critical is `High`. A protected volume whose latest recovery point is older than its own schedule is `High` (the backup may be failing). No cross-Region copy where the operator needs Regional disaster recovery is `Medium`. Unprotected non-critical volumes are `Low`.\\n\\n**Fix**: tag the volume to match an existing policy, add it to a backup selection, or create a policy. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Encryption posture\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault` and `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId` per Region.\\n2. Unencrypted volumes and snapshots (`Encrypted` is false).\\n3. For keys in use, AWS KMS `DescribeKey` state. A disabled or pending-deletion key in use is a risk.\\n4. Snapshot exposure: `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState` per Region, and `DescribeSnapshots --owner-ids self --restorable-by-user-ids all` for snapshots that are public now.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a key in use that is disabled or pending deletion is `High`. A public snapshot is `High`. Encryption by default off is `Medium`. Unencrypted volumes are `Medium`, or `High` if the operator says the data is regulated. Snapshot block public access in the `unblocked` state is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: turn on encryption by default; re-encrypt with the steps in [troubleshoot-encryption.md](troubleshoot-encryption.md); turn on snapshot block public access (`block-all-sharing`, or `block-new-sharing` while existing public shares are reviewed). All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Deletion protection\\n\\n**Checks**\\n\\n1. `DescribeInstanceAttribute --attribute blockDeviceMapping` for `DeleteOnTermination` on each attached volume. A data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is deleted when the instance terminates.\\n2. Recycle Bin `ListRules` for `EBS_SNAPSHOT` (and for AMIs if the account uses them).\\n3. Snapshot lock: `DescribeLockedSnapshots` for snapshots the operator must keep.\\n\\n**Rating rule**: a critical data volume with `DeleteOnTermination` true is `High`. No Recycle Bin rule for snapshots is `Medium`. No lock on snapshots the operator says are compliance records is `Medium`.\\n\\n**Fix**: `ModifyInstanceAttribute` to set `DeleteOnTermination` false on the data volume, a Recycle Bin retention rule, or a snapshot lock. All as directed-action proposals.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- Review mode is entirely read-only. It never runs a mutating call.\\n- Every fix is listed under \"Proposed actions\" in the report with exact parameters, expected effect, cost direction and rollback. Each one needs a directed action approved on the approval card.\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon EBS quotas: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/ebs-service.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-resource-quotas.html\\n- Requesting a quota increase: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicequotas/latest/userguide/request-quota-increase.html\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- gp3 and gp2: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/general-purpose.html\\n- Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-lifecycle.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/snapshot-ami-policy.html\\n- AWS Backup resource assignment: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/assigning-resources.html\\n- Encryption by default: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/encryption-by-default.html\\n- Block public access for snapshots: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html\\n- AWS Backup ListRecoveryPointsByResource: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/APIReference/API_ListRecoveryPointsByResource.html\\n- DeleteOnTermination: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/terminating-instances.html\\n- Recycle Bin: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/recycle-bin.html\\n- Snapshot lock: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-snapshot-lock.html\\n- Fast snapshot restore: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-fast-snapshot-restore.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_6b8MhPRExx2hDZswoP7Lo8", "content": "[{'text': '# Data collection: read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks\\n\\nLoad this file on every request. Every value in a verdict or a review comes from one of these calls. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency`, `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`. Nitro instances only |\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeReadOps`, `VolumeWriteOps`, `VolumeReadBytes`, `VolumeWriteBytes`, `VolumeTotalReadTime`, `VolumeTotalWriteTime`, `VolumeQueueLength`, `VolumeIdleTime`, `BurstBalance`, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` (Provisioned IOPS SSD only) | `VolumeId` |\\n| AWS/EC2 | `EBSIOBalance%`, `EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSReadOps`, `EBSWriteOps`, `EBSReadBytes`, `EBSWriteBytes` | `InstanceId` |\\n\\nMetric math from the Amazon CloudWatch metrics page for Amazon EBS. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average latency per operation = `VolumeTotalReadTime` / `VolumeReadOps` (and the write equivalent)\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. If they are absent, the instance does not publish them. That is not a fault.\\n\\n## Errors and fallbacks\\n\\n| What happens | What it means | What to do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `AccessDenied` on any call | The role cannot read that data | Name the exact API in Gaps. Continue with the rest |\\n| A read call is held behind an operator-approval gate (for example `dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies` or `rbin:ListRules`) | The Agent Space treats it as an action | Report it as a Gap and say which conclusion stays unconfirmed. Never ask the operator to bypass the gate |\\n| No `VolumeAvg*` data | The instance is not Nitro, or the `InstanceId` dimension is missing | Add `InstanceId`. If still empty, use the Sum-based math above |\\n| `EBSIOBalance%` absent | The instance size does not publish it | Compare the summed IOPS and MiB/s of all attached volumes to the `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline |\\n| `DescribeInstanceTypes` values in MB/s | The API reports instance throughput in MB/s (bandwidth in Mbps) | Convert to MiB/s before comparing (1 MB/s = 1,000,000 bytes/s; 1 MiB/s = 1,048,576 bytes/s) |\\n| AWS CloudTrail optional lookup denied or empty | No access, or the event is outside retention | Use `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the change record. It is not bound by AWS CloudTrail retention |\\n| No metric data for a volume | The volume is new, detached, or the window is wrong | Check `DescribeVolumes` state and attachment times, widen the window, report the Gap |\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- Instance metrics, including `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances (baseline and maximum, MB/s): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- AWS FIS actions: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fis/latest/userguide/fis-actions-reference.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_aCCVOCcpXDA3ExKbJrdHs8", "content": "[{'text': '# Finding logic: verdict template, binding layer, escalation, review ratings\\n\\n## Troubleshoot verdict template\\n\\nEvery troubleshoot answer uses these six headings in this order.\\n\\n1. **Answer.** The question the user asked, answered first in one or two sentences. For example \"Not stuck. The modification is in `optimizing`, which already applies the new IOPS.\"\\n2. **Evidence.** The values that support the answer, each with units and the time window (for example \"average `<value>` IOPS, `<start>` to `<end>` UTC\"). Throughput in MiB/s.\\n3. **Binding layer.** One of: Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment, Not applicable.\\n4. **Recommendation.** Exact parameters (volume ID, dimension, target value, how the target was computed), or \"No change\". Mutating steps are proposals for a directed action.\\n5. **Separate findings.** Other true facts, labelled so they never change the Answer. For example a modification that succeeded on a volume whose instance caps delivered IOPS: the cap goes here, never as \"the modification failed\".\\n6. **Gaps.** What could not be checked and why (API denied, approval gate, metric absent).\\n\\n## Binding-layer decision tree\\n\\nWork through it in order. Use measured values and the limits read from the APIs. Do not use fixed percentage triggers.\\n\\n1. Is the summed IOPS or MiB/s of all attached volumes flat at the instance EBS baseline, or are `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Instance**. Say \"the volume has headroom; raising volume IOPS will not help; change the instance type\". If a volume is also flat at its own limit, report both and fix the instance first, because volume changes cannot deliver above the instance ceiling.\\n2. Is the instance healthy and one volume flat at its own provisioned limit on the dimension its type is judged by?\\n   - Yes: **Volume**.\\n3. Is a gp2, st1 or sc1 volume\\'s `BurstBalance` draining or at 0?\\n   - Yes: **Burst credits**.\\n4. Did an operation fail on a quota (error text names a limit)?\\n   - Yes: **Quota**. Use the Capacity and quota headroom section of [review-operational.md](review-operational.md).\\n5. Are all layers below their limits, latency at the volume\\'s normal level, and queue length low?\\n   - Yes: **Not EBS**. Check CPU, memory, network and the application.\\n6. Are all layers below their limits but latency and `VolumeQueueLength` up while IOPS and throughput collapse?\\n   - Yes: **AWS-side impairment** (or injected latency). Never recommend more provisioning. Follow the escalation rules below.\\n\\n### Qualitative attribution matrix for \"is it storage?\"\\n\\nFrom the attribution draft, with the numeric CPU bands removed because no public source states them.\\n\\n| CPU | Volume latency | Queue length | Likely attribution |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| High | High | High | Application drives heavy I/O. Both compute and storage are stressed |\\n| High | Normal | Low | Compute, not storage |\\n| Low | High | High | Storage. The application waits on I/O. Go to the decision tree |\\n| Low | Normal | Low | Neither. Check network, locks and the application |\\n\\n\"High\" and \"normal\" mean compared with the same resource\\'s own history and the type\\'s documented expectation in [metrics-thresholds.md](metrics-thresholds.md).\\n\\n## Escalation (shared capability)\\n\\nEscalate to AWS Support when either is true:\\n\\n- Scope signals: an open AWS Health event for the volume, Availability Zone or Region; several resources failing the same way; `DescribeVolumeStatus` reports the volume as impaired or a failing status check.\\n- A bounded investigation cannot explain the symptom: all layers below limits, no running AWS FIS experiment, no recent change, and the symptom persists.\\n\\nSpecific cases:\\n\\n- Attach or detach stuck: the attachment stays in `attaching` or `detaching` and does not progress. Diagnose (instance state, device name, whether the volume is still mounted, any forced detach already tried), then escalate. A backend action can be needed.\\n- Modification in `optimizing` with `Progress` not increasing across several reads, or still optimizing after 24 hours. Tell the user the Amazon EBS User Guide says some performance changes take more than 24 hours, so this is a check, not a fault finding. Escalate with the evidence.\\n- Snapshot stuck in `pending` with no progress change over the same kind of window.\\n\\nEvidence pack to include:\\n\\n1. Account placeholder, Region, volume IDs, instance IDs, snapshot IDs as read from the APIs\\n2. The time window (first ALARM time, symptom start)\\n3. Metric evidence with units (IOPS, MiB/s, latency, queue length, `EBSIOBalance%`, `BurstBalance`)\\n4. Volume status and AWS Health results\\n5. `DescribeVolumesModifications` records, and AWS CloudTrail results if that optional lookup was available\\n6. What was ruled out and how\\n7. The Gaps list\\n\\n## Review ratings\\n\\nEach review finding has:\\n\\n| Field | Values |\\n|---|---|\\n| Severity | `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, or `Indeterminate` (the data could not be read) |\\n| Evidence | The values and API that show it |\\n| Fix | A specific change with parameters |\\n| Mutating? | Yes or No. Yes means the fix is a proposal for a directed action |\\n\\nRate by impact if the risk happens, not by count. Severity guidance per area is in [review-operational.md](review-operational.md). The report layout is in [review-report-format.md](review-report-format.md).\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Volume status checks: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-status.html\\n- Detaching volumes: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-detaching-volume.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Modification duration (more than 24 hours in some cases): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- Amazon EBS performance: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-performance.html\\n- Published S3 skill rating scale (format only): https://github.com/aws/tools-for-devops-agent\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}
